newsitem.title: USA: Buddhist temple repaid donors for 3 DNC events.
newsitem.headline: Buddhist temple repaid donors for 3 DNC events.

text.p: A Buddhist temple under investigation for making improper contributions to the 1996 presidential campaign repaid individuals who wrote checks to three Democratic fund-raisers, the Washington Post said Friday.

The newspaper quoted an internal Senate memorandum as saying the "donation-laundering" went beyond earlier reports that the Hsi Lai monastery in Hacienda Heights, California, repaid $58,000 to 12 donors at an April 1996 fund-raiser attended by Vice President Al Gore.

The memorandum said an additional $23,000 was chanelled through "similar Temple money-laundering" in connection with a February 1996 fund-raiser at the Hay Adams Hotel in Washington, and another $10,000 given at a DNC event in Los Angeles in July 1996.
It is illegal to finance a political donation officially listed in the name of another.

At least eight people wrote checks of $3,000 or $2,500 in connection with the Hay Adams fund-raiser after receiving checks from the temple for identical amounts, according to the memo, the Post reported.
At the Los Angeles fund-raiser, two others wrote checks for $5,000 after each received $5,000 checks from the temple the same day.
The memo was written by Michael Madigan, chief counsel for the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee.
